newsitem.title: UK: Deregulation of British casinos to start in April.
newsitem.headline: Deregulation of British casinos to start in April.

text.p: Britain's casinos will see the first fruits of government deregulation plans on April 3, when they will be allowed to keep bars open later and to admit new members more quickly, a Home Office minister said on Thursday.
Timothy Kirkhope said a parliamentary order which will take effect then would reduce the time a punter had to wait between applying to join a casino and gaming at its tables to 24 hours from 48.
The order will also free casinos from operating "pub hours" in their bars, allowing them to remain open until two in the morning in the provinces and three in London.

The casino industry has long demanded a revision of the waiting time for new members, arguing that it has discouraged businessmen and tourists in Britain for only a few days from visiting their tables.

Kirkhope said in a parliamentary written answer that the government planned to submit a further deregulation order to parliament after a favourable response to proposals it opened to public consultation.
These proposals included relaxation of an advertising ban, and allowing postal applications for membership.
However, Kirkhope said more work needed to be done on proposals to increase the number of slot machines allowed to three slot per gaming table.
He said further consideration was also needed before proposals to allow casinos in 21 new locations could go ahead.

"The changes that I wish to make could be implemented by secondary legislation. Before any new areas are introduced, however, I will need to address the resource, timing and other practical implications," he said.
He said he had slightly revised the list of locations after consultation with local authorities and others. -- London Newsroom +44 171 5427767
